physicalNotes: Radius 1.872 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 65109: radius 1.872 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 22.456 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.088) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 1,302,350 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Temperature 9191 +/- 421 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 65109: effective temperature 9191 +/- 421 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.034) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.

sources.position: Gaia DR3 source 6165699748417797504 (Gaia Collaboration 2023, A&A 674, A1), ICRS at epoch J2016.0, from the archived row src/objects/kulou/source/photometry/gaia-dr3-source.csv; cross-identification HD 115892, HR 5028, HIP 65109: https://simbad.cds.unistra.fr/simbad/sim-id?Ident=Gaia+DR3+6165699748417797504
sources.distance: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 65109: distance 18.021 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.003), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 18.021 +/- 0.054 pc; Gaia DR3 gives this source no parallax (a two-parameter solution)
sources.properMotion: Gaia DR3 source 6165699748417797504 is a two-parameter solution with no proper motion; zero is assumed (at 18 pc, 1 mas/yr would be 0 km/s across the sky)
sources.radialVelocity: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 6165699748417797504 (quality A), from 2006AstL...32..759G; Gaia DR3 measures none (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2006AstL...32..759G/abstract)
